ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are 8 numbered circles in the figure. It can be directly seen that circle 2 is connected to circle 5 and circle 6, and circle 5 is also connected to circle 6, so 2, 5, 6 form a triangle; it can also be seen that circle 2 is connected to circle 6 and circle 8, and circle 6 is also connected to circle 8, so 2, 6, 8 also form a triangle, and these two triangles share the edge 2-6. Reasoning: There are only three colors, red, yellow, and blue, and directly connected circles cannot have the same color. In any triangle, the three vertices are directly connected pairwise, so three different colors must be used respectively. In triangle 2-5-6, circle 5 must be the third color different from circle 2 and circle 6; in triangle 2-6-8, circle 8 also must be the third color different from circle 2 and circle 6. Because the colors of circle 2 and circle 6 are identically shared by the two triangles, circle 5 and circle 8 can only take the same remaining color. Therefore, the ones that must have the same color are circle 5 and circle 8.

raw_record.question_text: Prab painted each of the eight circles in the diagram red, yellow or blue such that no two circles that are joined directly were painted the same colour. Which two circles must have been painted the same colour?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a graph: circles 2, 5, and 6 are mutually joined, forming a triangle; circles 2, 6, and 8 are also mutually joined, forming another triangle sharing the edge 2-6. From the text, only three colours are available and directly joined circles must have different colours. Therefore each triangle must use all three colours. Since both triangles already share the same two colours on circles 2 and 6, their remaining vertices, circles 5 and 8, must each receive the third colour. Hence circles 5 and 8 must be the same colour.

method.method_draft: Focus on the joined pair 2 and 6 in the diagram. Because 2 and 6 are directly joined, the text rule forces them to have two different colours. Now read from the image that circle 5 is joined to both 2 and 6, and circle 8 is also joined to both 2 and 6. With only three colours available, any circle joined to both 2 and 6 cannot use either of their two colours, so it must use the only remaining colour. Therefore both circle 5 and circle 8 are forced to use that same remaining colour.
